page: Amazon Web Services t9g.small is an entry-level burstable instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 2 burstable vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, running single-threaded execution at 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 2.0 GB, yielding a 1.0 GB memory-to-core allocation. Like other members of the Nitro-based burstable family, the instance operates on shared CPU capacity designed to accumulate credits during low utilization periods and burst during elevated processing demand.

Hardware integration excludes dedicated GPUs and local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions such as EBS volumes for persistent disks. The instance features a baseline network throughput of 0 Gbps and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, operating entirely under the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Because this profile offers modest compute and limited memory, architectural tradeoffs involve low memory headroom and susceptibility to CPU throttling if burst capacity is depleted.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the t9g.small offers an economical hardware profile for light, intermittent workloads that do not maintain steady CPU loads. It is suited for low-traffic web microservices, light background workers, basic automation scripts, development environments, and small test environments that execute on ARM-native code bases.
